the NH2-terminal sequence of B. lichenformis penicillinse, when synthesized in E. Coli, contains covalently attached glyceride and palmitate, and that these results suggest the existence of a general system in E
the signal sequence of B. lichenformis penicillin is modified in E. coli to form glycerol-cysteine and that fatty acid is covalently bound to the glyceride residue.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a new modification system in E.coli, which is similar to the modification system that results in the formation in E. coli of glyceride-cys in the signal sequence in prolipoprotein.
the elucidation of the mechanism of penicillin resistance and with the development of new methods of controlling this resistance in the environment.
the elucidation of the mechanism of penicillin resistance in Gram-positive bacteria and with the biosynthetic modification of membrane proteins in Gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
penicillinase is synthesized in E. colli in the precursor form, which is covalently linked to glyceride and contains a fatty acid.

the signal peptide of the penicillin amidase precursor is modified by fatty acylation and glyceride formation, and the modified signal sequence is cleaved off from the penicillin amido beta-lactamhydolase precursor.
the NH2 termini of the lipoproteins of Gram-positive bacteria and the lipoprotein precursor of E. coli contain a fatty acid and glyceryl moiety covalently linked to cysteine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the signal sequence of a membrane protein of E. coli is not a random sequence, but is a specific signal for the formation of the NH2 termini of membrane proteins.

the signal sequence of B. lichenformis penicillinse contains the tetrapeptide Leu-Ala- Gly-Cys, and that the cysteine of the tetrapeptide is modified in E. coli to form glycerol-cysteine, which is the NH2 termini of B. lichemiformis penicillnase synthesized in E coli.
the NH2-terminal cysteine residue of penicillinases is modified by the addition of glyceride and/or fatty acid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the signal sequence of a membrane protein can be used to determine its fate.
the signal sequence is a key determinant of the post-translational modification of membrane proteins.
